issues.legal_issue: A state tax on land and buildings falls within the State Legislature’s competence when each property is taxed as a separate unit rather than as part of the owner’s combined assets.
material_facts: The original enactment imposed a tax on urban land.
A later amendment extended the tax to lands and buildings and included a proviso providing for assessment of multiple properties owned by the same person together.
A subsequent corrective amendment provided that tax would be levied on land or building, or both, separately as units.
The challenge concerned whether the resulting tax was within the State Legislature’s competence or was a tax on the owner’s total assets.
issues.conclusion: The charging provisions, as corrected, imposed a tax within the State Legislature’s competence over taxes on lands and buildings.
issues.legal_principle: Under Entry 49 of List II, a State Legislature may tax land and buildings as separate units, but not as a composite tax on their totality or as a tax concerned with the division of ownership or occupation interests. The Court relied on Union of India v. H.S. Dhillon and D.C. Gouse & Co. v. State of Kerala; it distinguished a tax on property under Entry 49 of List II from a tax on total assets under Entry 86 of List I.

rule.if: state_tax_challenge and properties_taxed_as_separate_units and not combined_asset_tax and not ownership_interest_division_tax

predicates.state_tax_challenge: A party challenges the constitutional validity of a tax imposed by a state legislature.
predicates.properties_taxed_as_separate_units: The tax is imposed on each item of land or building as a separate unit.
predicates.combined_asset_tax: The tax is imposed on the combined total value of a person’s lands and buildings as a whole.
predicates.ownership_interest_division_tax: The tax depends on how ownership or occupation of the land or building is divided among persons.
predicates.tax_within_state_legislative_competence: The tax falls within the state legislature’s competence to tax land and buildings.

issues.definition: When a state tax challenge concerns a tax on property taxed as separate units, and not a combined-asset tax or an ownership-interest-division tax, the tax is within state legislative competence.

issues.legal_issue: An invalid portion of an amended statute may be severed when the valid remainder is complete and workable, and the original enactment can remain valid independently of the defective amendment.
material_facts: The original enactment imposed a tax on urban land and was within the State Legislature’s competence.
A later amendment introduced provisions that could operate as a tax on the combined value of a person’s lands and buildings.
A subsequent corrective amendment retrospectively omitted the offending proviso and clarified that properties were taxed separately as units.
The remaining provisions formed a workable scheme without the omitted proviso.
issues.conclusion: The offending portion was severable, and the remaining charging and supporting provisions were valid and workable.
issues.legal_principle: Whether valid and invalid parts are severable depends on legislative intention, including whether the legislature would have enacted the valid part without the invalid part. If the valid provisions are distinct and form a complete code after the invalid portion is removed, they may stand; if the provisions are inextricably mixed, the whole enactment fails. The Court relied on M.P.V. Sundara Ramaiar and Co. v. State of Andhra Pradesh and R.M.D. Chamarbaugwalla v. Union of India.

rule.if: statute_validity_challenge and defective_part_separable and valid_remainder_complete_and_workable and original_enactment_independently_valid

predicates.statute_validity_challenge: A party challenges the validity of a statute containing both valid and defective parts.
predicates.defective_part_separable: The defective part can be removed without making the remaining provisions dependent on it.
predicates.valid_remainder_complete_and_workable: After the defective part is removed, the remaining provisions form a complete and workable scheme.
predicates.original_enactment_independently_valid: The enactment before the defective amendment was itself within the legislature’s competence.
predicates.valid_remainder_remains_enforceable: The valid remainder continues to have legal effect and may be enforced.

issues.definition: When a statute is challenged, a separable defective part may be removed while a complete and workable remainder remains enforceable, particularly where the original enactment was independently valid.

issues.legal_issue: A defective amendment does not make an independently valid enactment permanently still-born when a corrective amendment removes the defect retrospectively before a court declares the enactment invalid.
material_facts: The original enactment was independently valid and had not yet been brought into operation when the later amendment introduced the defect.

Before a court had declared the enactment invalid, a corrective ordinance and replacement enactment retrospectively removed the offending provision and clarified the tax’s operation on separate units.
The provisions remaining after correction formed a complete and workable scheme.
issues.conclusion: The original enactment was not still-born; the retrospective corrective measure restored the enforceability of the valid scheme, and the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: A legislature may correct an amendment that exceeds its competence where the valid original enactment can stand independently and the defective portion is severable. A valid and complete remainder survives removal of the defect; the Court distinguished M/s. West Ramnad Electric Distribution Co. Ltd. v. State of Madras and Mahendra Lal Jaini v. State of Uttar Pradesh, which did not prevent the legislature from correcting its error before a judicial verdict.

rule.if: challenge_to_amended_enactment and original_enactment_independently_valid and defect_introduced_by_later_amendment and retrospective_correction_before_judicial_invalidation and corrected_remainder_complete_and_workable

predicates.challenge_to_amended_enactment: A party challenges an enactment as amended by a later legislative measure.
predicates.original_enactment_independently_valid: The enactment before the later amendment was itself within the legislature’s competence.
predicates.defect_introduced_by_later_amendment: The defect arose from a subsequent amendment rather than from the original enactment.
predicates.retrospective_correction_before_judicial: The legislature retrospectively corrected the defect before a court declared the enactment invalid.
predicates.corrected_remainder_complete_and_workabl: After correction, the remaining provisions form a complete and workable scheme.
predicates.corrected_enactment_remains_enforceable: The enactment, as corrected, continues to have legal effect and may be enforced.

issues.definition: If an independently valid enactment is made defective by a later amendment, and a retrospective correction made before judicial invalidation leaves a complete and workable scheme, the corrected enactment remains enforceable.
